text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Belgrade students continue protests, they are now gathering in the pedestrian Knez Mihajlova street.
- The Yugoslav government 1997 economic policy priorities are maintaining a stable dinar exchange rate and prices through market measures.

- Yugoslav army general staff issued a statement saying it continues to be a factor for social stability and guarantor of the sovereignty, integrity and security of the country and of all its citizens.
- Serbian power company EPS introduced power cuts from Monday because of large electricity consumption, appeals on consumers to save energy.
- Opposition coalition Zajedno leaders call Belgraders to celebrate new Year's Eve on the town's main square where protests have been going on for over a month.
- Protests over annullment of local election results continue in other towns of Serbia - Nis, Sremska Mitrovica, Negotin, Kragujevac etc.
- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic says he has normal communication with Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic denying opposition reports to the contrary.
- The Holy Synod of the Serbian Orthodox church to hold a meeting on January 2 to discuss the citizens' protests throughout Serbia.
